chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He (peace be upon him) disliked that game be shot while it is heading towards the Sanctuary (Mecca).

key_terms.الصَّيْدُ: game, wild animals hunted for food or sport
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the Sanctuary, specifically referring to Mecca and its sacred precincts
key_terms.يَأُمُّ: heading towards, leading to (in the context of movement/direction)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting game while it is flying towards Mecca during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual sensitivity of the Haram boundaries, where the act of hunting is discouraged not merely as a legal prohibition but as a matter of preserving the tranquility and sanctity of the sacred space. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the broader principle that the Haram is a domain of peace, where physical disturbances like hunting are minimized to enhance the pilgrim's spiritual focus. The dislike (karahah) indicates a recommended precaution rather than a strict invalidation of the hunt, emphasizing reverence for the sanctuary.
